qs.q: Human errors:
o: Are now considered as being inherent to the cognitive function of human and can be totally eliminated by CRM training.
Are now considered as being inherent to the cognitive function of human and are generally inescapable.
Are likely to be eliminated in the near future by higher degree of automation.

qs.q: The error in checklist is related to an interface mismatch between:
o: Liveware - Liveware.
Liveware - Software.
Liveware - Environment.
qs.ex: Checklists, manuals and charts are Software.

qs.q: CRM training has under mentioned clear aims in terms of specific skills to develop for the purpose of:
o: Error avoidance, threat management, system management and undesired aircraft state management.
Error avoidance, threat management, error management and environment management.
Error avoidance, threat management, error management and undesired aircraft state management.

qs.q: A congested cockpit restricting movement is an interface mismatch between:
o: Liveware - Software.
Liveware - Environment.
Liveware - Hardware.

qs.q: High noise level in a cockpit is a mismatch between:
o: Liveware - Liveware.
Liveware - Environment.
Liveware - Hardware.

qs.q: A disturbance of the biological rhythm is a mismatch between:
o: Liveware - Hardware.
Liveware - Software.
Liveware - Environment.
qs.ex: Time of day and time zones are part of the Environment.

qs.q: The main consideration in modern airline operations should be:
o: Efficient utilisation of resources.
Maximum utilisation of resources.
Safety.

qs.q: The elements of the SHEL model are:
o: Software, hardware, electronics and liveware.
Shareware, hardware, education and limitations.
Software, hardware, environment and liveware.

qs.q: Which is true regarding the interaction between various elements of the SHEL model?
o: All components of the SHEL model are equally important, as conflict and error can arise from the various mismatches.
The hardware is the hub for interactions between the different components of the system, hence other components should be matched to design most suitable hardware.
The liveware is the hub of the SHEL model; therefore, the nonhuman components should be adapted and matched to this central component.

qs.q: CRM and LOFT training are designed to improve:
o: The quality number of individuals performance.
Individual performance in adverse conditions.
The quality of crew performance.

qs.q: Four important disciplines from which information is drawn in understanding human performance and behavior are:
o: Psychology, engineering, physiology, and anthropometry.
Sociology, mathematics, biology and industrial design.
Physics, biochemistry, physiology, and anthropometry.

qs.q: Pilots have now become responsible for the management of hardware and software interfaces, through which they are required to direct the operation of the aircraft. These technological advances have:
o: Significantly eliminated human errors.
Given rise to new forms of error.
Are aimed to eliminate pilots from the cockpit.

qs.q: About what proportion of civil air accidents result from inadequate human performance?
What is meant by the trans authority gradient?
o: It is the authority exercised by the captain over all flight operations.
It is the authority relationship between captain and other crew members.
It is the authority relationship between captain and first officer.

qs.q: Introducing Automation in a cockpit:
o: Always reduces potential for human error and workload.
Generally relocates potential for error and increases workload.
Eliminates human error but work load increases.

qs.q: High arousal overload results in:
o: A real danger of attention becoming narrowed.
Attention becoming sharpest.
An optimum arousal for more difficult or intellectual (cognitive) tasks.

qs.q: A pilot suffering from a mild head ache before flight can:
o: Take Over The Counter medicines from the chemist and fly.
Take Over The Counter medicines from the first aid box in the aircraft and fly.
Should take medicines prescribed by an aviation medicine specialist and take his advise for flying.

qs.q: Categories of errors defined by TEM are:
o: Intentional non-compliance error, Procedural error, Communication error, Proficiency error and Operational decision error.
Intentional non-compliance error, Procedural error, Communication error, Proficiency error and vigilance error.
Instrument error, Procedural error, Communication error, Proficiency error and vigilance error.

qs.q: Operational threats outside the control of the flight crew are:
o: Adverse weather, terrain, airport conditions, heavy traffic/TCAS events, unfamiliar airports etc.
Time pressure, irregular operations, flight diversions, missed approaches etc.
Aircraft malfunctions, automation events etc.
qs.ex: Option A lists environmental threats and C aircraft threats; operational threats are time pressure, diversions, missed approaches.

qs.q: What airplane equipment marked a substantial decrease in hull loss rates in the eighties?
o: GPWS
TCAS
SSR
